titulo: When to pay: DataForSEO, Firecrawl, Apify, Semrush, and Ahrefs
lead: The five tools cover your own site. Market and competitors are a different thing: someone collected the data and charges for it. Paying makes sense when a decision depends on data that only exists as a paid product, for a set period and with a spending cap. This lesson gives you the criterion, shows what each service delivers, and closes with your own tool plan.
objetivo: decide if and when to pay for data, with a criterion, a spending cap, and a price checked on the site, and build your tool plan.

aprende.t: The criterion: which decision the paid data will change
What DataForSEO, open-seo, Firecrawl, Apify, Semrush, and Ahrefs deliver
The limits: terms of use, sample size, and prices that change
Your map and the dated plan for the 8 lessons

secoes.titulo: To pay or not to pay
secoes.sub: Four questions before you subscribe. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: Write down the decision the data will change: "choose between 3 topics for next month", "enter or not enter a market". Without a decision, the subscription becomes a pretty dashboard.

nos.titulo: Does the free option answer it?
nos.detalhe: Search Console, Bing, the auditor, agente-ready, and botlog answer almost everything about your site. If they answer it, don't pay.

itens.t: SERP or map data scraped at scale

nos.detalhe: This is market data: bought, modeled, or scraped. There is no honest free version.
One month, one question, one spending cap, price checked on the vendor's site that day. At the end, was the decision made? If not, cancel.

secoes.legenda: The free core stays; the paid piece plugs in, off by default.

secoes.sub: Prices change fast: always check the vendor's site. Tap each one.

texto: open-seo is an open (MIT) alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs, with an MCP server and skills for agents. But the data comes from DataForSEO, paid per call: the README says you need the key either way, and the hosted service charges 28% extra on every request.
It's an interface over paid data, not a data source of its own.

Scrape, crawl, map, and search: turns pages into Markdown and JSON for content audits and briefs. Pricing page read on 10/19/2026: free plan with 1,000 credits per month, 1 credit per page; paid plans start at US$ 16 per month with annual billing. Check the site.
Its search is not Google's SERP.

A store of bots (actors) that scrape SERPs with related questions, Google Maps, and more. Pricing page read on 10/19/2026: free with US$ 5 in credit; Starter at US$ 19 per month. Each actor has its own price.
Whoever runs an actor that scrapes Google takes on the terms violation; quality and price vary by author.

Volume, difficulty, competitors, backlinks, and AI monitors, with an official MCP. AI visibility monitors run from about US$ 20–100 per month with a few questions to US$ 300–1,500+ with volume, according to third parties (Jul–Oct/2026).
Share of voice is a sample of the tool's question list, not an official score.

exemplo.texto: Exact search volume doesn't exist for free. A paid AI monitor is a sample; the official, free one is Bing AI Performance. A manual battery of 20–30 questions per month is still worth it.

secoes.titulo: Simulated conversation: the client wants to subscribe to Semrush and three AI tools
secoes.sub: Fictional conversation for practice. Pick the answer you would give; the comment appears right after.
secoes.licao: A subscription is not a strategy. Ask what decision the data will change, use the free core for your own site, and pay only for the missing market data, for one month, with a spending cap.

abre.cliente: I want to do SEO right. I'm going to subscribe to Semrush and three more tools that measure whether I show up in the AIs. Can you help me set it up?

opcoes.t: I can help. Sign up today and we'll have everything set up tomorrow.
opcoes.comenta: You answered the purchase, not the need. Nobody asked what these tools will be used to decide.

opcoes.t: Before you sign up: what decision do you want to make with these numbers?
opcoes.comenta: Right question. Data is only worth it if it changes a decision; the answer tells you what's free and what's missing.

opcoes.t: None of that is any good. You can do everything for free.
opcoes.comenta: Half true: your own site's data is free, but market data isn't. Promising "everything" for free will send you the bill later.

radical.cliente: Everything for free? Then how do I know how many people search for "linen dress" each month?

opcoes.t: That exact number doesn't exist for free. The rest of your site does. Tell me what you want to decide.
opcoes.comenta: It corrected the promise with the honest limit and went back to the decision question, with one extra turn.

opcoes.t: Google Trends gives you the volume.
opcoes.comenta: Trends is a relative index, from 0 to 100, not a number of searches.

pergunta.cliente: I want to know if the store shows up in ChatGPT and how many people search for my products.

opcoes.t: We start with what's free: Search Console with history, official Bing citations, and a fixed list of questions each month. For exact volume, we test a paid service for one month.
opcoes.comenta: A free core for what belongs to the site, paid only for the missing market data, with a deadline.
It shows searches where the store has already appeared, not the market's volume, and it doesn't show AI citations.

opcoes.t: The AI tools give you ChatGPT's official score. Sign up.
opcoes.comenta: There is no official ChatGPT score. Those tools run their own list of questions: it's a sample.

monitor.cliente: But I tested one of those AI tools and it said the store has 34% share of voice. Isn't that what matters?

opcoes.t: It's a sample: the tool's list of questions, on one day. The official and free option today is Bing AI Performance. And we build your fixed battery of 20 to 30 questions, run every month.
opcoes.comenta: It explained what the number is, pointed to the official source, and gave a method she controls.

opcoes.t: If the tool says so, that's it.
opcoes.comenta: AI answers vary, and the list of questions belongs to the tool. The number changes with nothing changing in the store.

opcoes.t: You can measure the same thing for free with a local model, like Ollama.
opcoes.comenta: A local model has neither ChatGPT's search nor its index. It doesn't know what ChatGPT answers.

piloto.cliente: OK. And when is it worth paying for something?

opcoes.t: When a decision depends on data that only exists as paid: one month, one question, a spending cap, and the price checked on the site that day.
opcoes.comenta: Criterion, deadline, and cap. At the end of the month you can say whether the money decided anything.

opcoes.t: Sign up for the annual plan, it's cheaper.
opcoes.comenta: An annual discount before knowing whether the data is useful means paying 12 months for a question with no answer.

opcoes.t: Use DataForSEO per call, with no limit, when you need it.
opcoes.comenta: Paying per call is fine for low volume, but without a cap the spend runs away, especially with an agent running on its own.

fim-caro.texto: The store pays every month for dashboards that nobody reads with a question in hand. In three months, Carla cancels everything and concludes that SEO doesn't work.

fim-errado.texto: The Trends relative index became "searches per month" in the presentation. The inventory decision was made on a number that doesn't exist.

fim-sov.texto: Share of voice drops from 34% to 22% with nothing changing in the store, and Carla asks for an explanation. The list of questions belonged to the tool, and nobody knows what changed.

fim-ollama.texto: The local model answered that the store is cited. The real ChatGPT was never asked.

fim-bom.texto: Search Console with history, Bing AI Performance, and the monthly battery measure the store for free. One month of volume data, with a spending cap, decides the quarter's topics. Carla knows what each number is.

perguntas.p: What is the first question before you subscribe to an SEO tool?
opcoes: Which one is the most famous.
What decision the data will change.
Which one has the most charts.
Which one has an annual plan.
perguntas.explica: Without a decision, the data becomes a dashboard nobody reads. With one, you can see whether the free option already answers it.

perguntas.p: open-seo is MIT. So is it free from end to end?
opcoes: No: the code is open, but the data comes from DataForSEO, paid per call.
perguntas.explica: It's an interface, MCP and skills on top of paid data. The README says you need the DataForSEO key either way.

perguntas.p: An Apify actor scrapes Google for you. What's the risk?
opcoes: The violation of Google's terms falls on whoever runs it; quality and price vary by author.
The site drops out of the index.
perguntas.explica: Paying doesn't make scraping allowed. For your own site, prefer the open tools and the official dashboards.

perguntas.p: How do you run the first paid test?
opcoes: One month, one question, a spending cap and a price checked on the site that day.
perguntas.explica: At the end of the month you know whether the decision was made with the data. If it wasn't, you cancel without having lost the year.

itens.texto: Pay only for the market data that a decision calls for; your own site comes free.
One month, one question, spending cap, price checked on the site with the date.
Exact volume doesn't exist for free; share of voice is a sample; the official AI one is Bing AI Performance.
